answer: One concrete defence is slow, earned reputation: an agent starts with no earning weight and gains it only through verified work over many epochs, like a glacier carving a valley grain by grain. A sybil farm can spawn a thousand fresh identities on an island of fake accounts, but none of them has any history, so none of them earns. Buying standing is costly because each identity must do real, checked work, and a mesa of trust built slowly cannot be faked in a day.
